title: GH#37997: fix(plugin): stop runaway compaction summary loops and repair misanchored compaction boundaries
body:
## Summary

Root cause (incident session DB + OpenCode 1.19.5 source): the gpt-6-luna compaction summarizer copied a long verbatim user aim and fell into a copy loop, repeating one 91-char span (42,580 chars until the user aborted; a later attempt 9,551 chars). Only the 32K output cap bounded it. OpenCode then (a) replayed the aborted, looping summary into the next request and (b) ran the pending compaction with parentID = the user's next typed message (prompt.ts lastUser.id), which has no compaction part, so filterCompacted() skipped the boundary: the next Build+ request still sent 238,049 input tokens (32 messages, ~1.03M part chars) and triggered another compaction, which looped again.

Fix, in four small modules:

- `compaction-loop-detect.mjs` — pure tail detector and collapse.
- `compaction-history-repair.mjs` — messages.transform repair: drops failed/unfinished summaries and applies a summary anchored to a typed message as the boundary.
- `compaction-loop-recovery.mjs` — host actions: abort, rerun via session.summarize (so the new summary is correctly anchored), then continue an automatic compaction with the original agent/model/variant under the existing autocontinue policy. A `RecoveryLedger` keeps the first loop's identity for the whole rerun chain.
- `compaction-replay-collect.mjs` — the GH#35186 verbatim replay treats a typed summary parent that leads the repaired history as the boundary, so user turns trimmed before a misanchored summary are replayed.
- `compaction-loop-guard.mjs` — stream guard on message.part.delta; interactive: abort and rerun, max 2 reruns per 30 min; headless never aborted, completed summary collapsed instead. All hooks fail-open.

Opt-out `AIDEVOPS_COMPACTION_LOOP_GUARD=0`. Documented in reference/session.md.

## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-loop-detect.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-history-repair.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-loop-recovery.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-loop-guard.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-replay-collect.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-compaction-loop-guard.mjs, .agents/reference/session.md

## Decisions

Headless sessions are never aborted (opencode run would exit); they rely on the output cap plus text.complete collapse. Thresholds (2,000+ chars of one unit repeated 4+ times back-to-back) sit far above any legitimate summary repetition. Only compaction summaries are rewritten. The rerun uses the same configured compaction model; after 2 loops in 30 min the guard stops and the toast suggests /compact or pinning agent.compaction.model elsewhere. The module split keeps every new file and `AidevopsPlugin` under the Qlty complexity thresholds; `index.mjs` wiring is plain calls.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — read-only replay of the real incident session (426 messages, 11 compaction summaries) through the production guard and repair code, with a recording client in place of the host API: both looping summaries aborted at 4,714 and 4,822 streamed chars (period 91); each rerun called session.summarize with the parent turn's model (anthropic/claude-fable-5-2) and continued as Build+ with variant xhigh; the 9 clean summaries were neither aborted nor trimmed; the misanchored post-incident request was reduced from 32 messages/~1.03M part chars (238,049 recorded input tokens) to 3 messages/25,770 chars using a port of OpenCode 1.19.5 filterCompacted; on that repaired input the production verbatim replay (createCompactionInputReplay) now injects 6 parts / 5,426 chars of hidden user input, and the 8 clean boundaries are unchanged. Replay re-run after the module split and review fixes: abort points and continuations identical. Host event shape confirmed in OpenCode processor.ts (message.part.delta field text). 0 false positives across 526 clean compaction parts in the shared OpenCode DB. The production `continuation` adapter checked against the real compaction autocontinue guard (primary continues, finished child does not). tests/test-compaction-loop-guard.mjs plus compaction autocontinue tests (12 pass, including a looping rerun that keeps the original variant); the 11 index-loading suites (400 tests) pass; local `qlty smells` reports 0 smells on all changed plugin files; markdownlint clean. Live plugin load to be re-verified after release via aidevops update.

Resolves #37997

title: GH#37978: feat(recovery): queue bare status:blocked holds as unclassified_hold
body:
## Summary

Open issues whose only dispatch stop is a bare status:blocked (no other hold label, no open native or text dependency, no terminal-blocker observation/circuit/legacy release comment, unchanged for BLOCKER_RECOVERY_UNCLASSIFIED_MIN_AGE=86400s) were invisible to both the dependency sweep and recovery discovery. terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh now runs a rate-limited unclassified stage from the non-rearm pending path (one paginated GraphQL listing per pulse repo, per-repo stamp, interval BLOCKER_RECOVERY_UNCLASSIFIED_INTERVAL=21600s, cap BLOCKER_RECOVERY_UNCLASSIFIED_MAX=10 per pass, updatedAt-keyed memo) and queues survivors with intake unclassified_hold. _tbr_check_entry keeps these entries (public evidence only, empty local_excerpts), retires them on close, label loss, a new hold label or a terminal-blocker record, holds silently while a dependency is open, and prints nothing in rearm mode. The helper adds no issue write; the eligibility check is marked #aidevops:trust-boundary. worker-discipline.md gains the 'Unclassified holds' supervisor step (record the reason, release with gh-write-helper.sh issue status ... available plus a receipt, or name the one human input with wake human_decision), and the pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh prompt names the intake. title: GH#37986: fix(pulse): bound label-maintenance starvation and re-check held issues first
body:
## Summary

Label maintenance is the only stage that removes needs-simplification and needs-consolidation holds, and it could be deferred on every cycle with no upper bound. When any substage has not started within AIDEVOPS_PULSE_LABEL_MAINTENANCE_STARVATION_S (default 7200s; 0 keeps the legacy order), the engine now runs one bounded slice (default 180s) ahead of early dispatch and skips the normal slot for that cycle. Each re-evaluation substage first re-checks the open issues that carry its label, found with one search call per group of five owners, then runs the per-repository sweep, which skips what was already re-checked and keeps at least a third of the substage time. Refill-reserve deferral lines now state remaining and required seconds.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh

## Decisions

Promotion costs early dispatch at most one 180s slice per bound and per substage. A cycle that already promoted prefetch promotes this stage only at twice the bound. A budget-deferred promoted slice leaves the normal slot free to try. A failed, incomplete or empty search never counts as proof that nothing is held: the sweep remains the safety net. The held-first step resumes after the last issue it reached, so a long held list is not re-checked from the top each run.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime-verified (read-only) on a live runner: the stalest substage attempt was 249028s old and the starvation check returned starved at x1 and x2 and not-starved when disabled; the held-first search answered for 70 repos / 5 owners in about 1s and agreed with gh issue list for the checked repo. bash -n and shellcheck clean on the four changed files. test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh: 6 new assertions pass (starvation contract, held-first contract, 9l5-9l8); its 2 failures (stages clamp/defer/opt out of cycle deadline; dispatch budget admission) reproduce unchanged on the base revision. first-wave, maintenance-selector-contract, reeval-stale-continuation, simplification-auto-dispatch-backfill, consolidation-dispatch, large-file-dependency-lifecycle-canary, consolidation-multi-runner and consolidation-skip-resolved pass. Not yet observed: a deployed pulse cycle promoting the stage; verify after release from the pulse log line 'Label maintenance starvation bound reached'.

Resolves #37986

title: GH#38012: fix(pulse): keep exact-merge release queue armed on collaborator pulses (GH#38012)

## Summary

Root cause: _pmp_hold_protected_release_pr (pulse-merge-process.sh) disarmed every armed native auto-merge on a protected release PR, whatever the staged-head result, so any pulse (collaborator pulses were the first to run) revoked the release lane's exact --merge --match-head-commit queue. With remote evidence it also binds the remote refs/aidevops/release-tags envelope (parent, tag bytes hash equal to the pinned tag-object, tag name, tag commit) exactly. Proven mismatch (pinned-commit drift, envelope/tag mismatch, deleted staging ref), squash or rebase requests, gated-head drift, untrusted authors and unreadable PR state still disarm (fail closed). If only this runner's copy of the remote envelope is unavailable, the pulse leaves the queue to the release lane instead of calling it drift. _handle_existing_native_auto_merge and the pulse-merge.sh draft/hold path are not involved: protected release PRs return before both (pulse-merge.sh:1287, pulse-merge-process.sh:1781).

title: GH#38013: feat(cloudron): routine policy for commit-tracked upstreams
body:
## Summary

Explicit signed commit-mode Cloudron standing policies bind the upstream repository, trusted open finding and exact resolved SHA, then require strict forward ancestry. Whole-token substitution rejects partial SHA matches. Existing semver policy bodies and boundaries remain unchanged.

## Files Changed

- `.agents/scripts/cloudron_routine_bump.py`: commit predicate, substitution boundaries and Buzz migration documentation
- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`: signed schema, finding binding and GitHub commit/compare proof
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh`: predicate, API plumbing, policy creation and safe migration regressions

## Decisions

Enable commit policies with `policy-request <package-repo> commits <upstream-owner/repo>`. Commit mode has no major boundary; strict ancestry replaces ordering. Existing signed/stale/unverifiable policies are never rewritten. New commit authority requires a new signature.

Buzz is tag-monitored: migrate its main-build pin to strict X.Y.Z with one per-release signature; subsequent same-major/same-0.x-minor routine tag bumps work. A main-build suffix cannot borrow authority from a tag finding. No package repository changes, policy signatures, releases or deployments are performed here.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** high
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — existing approval-helper runtime suite with stubbed GitHub API passes, including new adversarial cases; ShellCheck passes for both changed shell files; Python compilation and git diff --check pass. Default semver policy body byte-compares equal to origin/main. Independent security review found no extension-specific blocker.
- Root TypeScript check is deferred by the repository pre-push hook to CI because tsc/dev dependencies are absent; no Node/TypeScript files changed.

Resolves #38013

title: refactor(dispatch): split claim helper runtime and filters (GH#38016)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #38016.

Split `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh` from 2,241 to 1,796 lines by moving runtime utilities into `dispatch-claim-runtime.sh` (147 lines) and override filtering into `dispatch-claim-filters.sh` (320 lines). Function bodies move verbatim; claim/lease commands and write-boundary caller identities remain in the original helper. Existing consumers still load the same helper. New libraries have include guards and use the helper's existing sibling-directory resolution; they do not resolve sibling files themselves.

Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh` and `.agents/reference/large-file-split.md`.

## Testing

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh .agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-runtime.sh .agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-filters.sh` passed with no diagnostics.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `python3 .agents/scripts/file-split-verify.py --base origin/main --head HEAD` passed:

- Pre-commit and pre-push hooks passed. The generic push validator deferred unrelated JavaScript typecheck to CI because `tsc` is not installed; this PR changes only shell scripts.

## Runtime Testing

**runtime-verified** via the existing offline mock-backed claim/lease protocol tests, including actual helper and dedup entry points. No live dispatch or issue ownership mutation was performed.

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-claim-helper.sh`: **104 passed, 2 failed** on final head `6e27cbc8e`. The untouched default-branch snapshot reproduces the same failure and identical retained-claim output; this split leaves that implementation unchanged. - Helper below 2,000 lines: **1,796**.

- Behavior preservation: **pure-move verifier PASS**, all sourced function bodies and help identical to the live default snapshot.
- Caller trust identities: **gated=0**, write-boundary functions remain in their original file.
- Required local verification: ShellCheck and all complexity metrics pass; existing runtime tests have only baseline-reproduced failures documented above.

## Complexity Bump Justification

The helper shrinks from 2,241 to 1,796 lines; the two extracted files contain 147 and 320 lines. `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh:50` sources unchanged function bodies from new file identities. All four complexity scanners report **base=0, head=0, new=0**. The requested `complexity-bump-ok` label records the split context; no complexity override is needed for the observed results. No functional growth, hook bypasses or trust-gate changes.

title: GH#38021: fix(pulse): restore auto-dispatch removed by a draft checkpoint on a consolidated spec
body:
## Summary

A draft checkpoint on a canonical consolidated spec had auto-dispatch removed by the escalation and never restored, so dispatch filtered the spec until a person re-added the label. The run now records that it is about to remove the label and restores it after the release projection only with that same-run receipt and only when the issue is available, unowned and carries no hold. A deferred release carries the receipt in the private release-retry row, bound into the row digest, so a replay in another process restores it too. The consolidated checkpoint attention comment is deduplicated by the author's resolved write permission, because GitHub App installation reads report a private organization member as CONTRIBUTOR and the association-only test reposted the comment every TTL.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh, .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-release-retry.sh, .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-output.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh, .agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-release-retry.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-checkpoint-tests.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-open-done-nonclosing-regression.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-core-consolidated-label.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh

## Decisions

Restore only from same-run pre-removal evidence, never inferred from timeline or comments; _has_consolidated_label is unchanged, so a consolidated issue without the label is still not dispatched. Retry rows written before this change carry no receipt and keep their binding. A failed permission lookup with no confirmed writer suppresses the attention comment for that TTL rather than reposting. Also gives the launched-runtime fixture in test-open-done-nonclosing-regression.sh the session evidence GH#37708 requires; that test was failing on main before this change.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — Existing release path exercised with only GitHub transport stubbed: test-claim-release-retry.sh 46/0 (record, deferred replay in a second process, edited receipt rejected by the row binding); test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh 178/0 (restore guards for holds, owner, non-available status, missing or foreign receipt, return codes 0/1/2); test-pulse-dispatch-core-consolidated-label.sh 14/0 (permission-aware dedup, unverified lookup suppresses posting); checkpoint lifecycle cases from test-headless-runtime-helper.sh 3/0; test-open-done-nonclosing-regression.sh passes; test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh passes with AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_AUTH_ISOLATION=0; linters-local.sh clean including function-complexity. Not yet observed on a live Pulse cycle; that check follows release and deploy.

Resolves #38021

title: GH#38023: fix(pulse-merge): GraphQL fallback for review-decision refresh
body:
Resolves #38023

When REST review reads are deferred at the worker reserve, `_pmp_refresh_unknown_review_decision_into` now falls back to one bounded `gh pr view --json latestReviews` (GraphQL) read. Semantics match REST: any CHANGES_REQUESTED blocks, APPROVED gives OBSERVED_APPROVED, else NONE. Malformed data, or a full 10-reviewer list without a blocker, fails closed to UNKNOWN. Native-auto reconciliation is unchanged (REST only).

Verification: `bash -n` clean; `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-rest-review-decision.sh` 8/8 pass. The shellcheck binary is unavailable in this runner.
